### LINE 1 — the frames: CONFIRMED (fixed, pinned)

Read whole: `kernel/src/tx/frames.ts` (405 lines) and the base → tree diffs of `tx/tx.ts`, `tx/savepoint.ts`,
`tx/state.ts`, `tx/index.ts` (`check-M0-a-06/scope/tx_*.diff`).

* `mark(t)` pushes a `Frame {batch, pos, arena: markArena(p), index: markIndex(idx)}` on the batch's stack (refused on
  an ended batch); `undoTo(t, m)` — refusals first, each a throw before anything is written: `m.batch !== b || !b.open`
  → `tx: an undo to a frame of another batch (a frame is undone only inside its own batch)`; `b.stack[m.pos] !== m` →
  `tx: an undo to a frame already undone or discarded (a frame is undone at most once, the frames after it with it)`;
  then `discardAbove(b, m.pos)` (m and every later frame leave the stack BEFORE the entries are undone), `undoArena`
  (S8's, unchanged: apply-then-cut per entry, then the saved counters, holesTop, version, frame, three kinds of count),
  then `undoIndex`. A dropped frame stays on the stack until an older undo or the batch's end (`discardAbove(b, 0)` in
  `undoBatch` / `endBatch`). The version is put back by value from the mark (the batch's own), the generation is never
  touched (frames.ts imports nothing of savepoint.ts).
* THE BATCH FRAME: `markBatch(p)` (throws if a recorder is still attached; `attachRecorder`; the mark) is called only
  from `tx.ts` `open` — after every declaration check and, new in this round, after both `rankOf` calls (the author's
  N-s9-6: a stage with no u8 rank used to throw with the index log left open) — and BEFORE `beginIndexBatch`;
  `undoBatch(b)` only from `reject`, the catch and the batch that wrote nothing (grep: tx.ts:142, :558, :608), each
  ending with `idx.log = null` and `detachRecorder`; `endBatch(b)` only at the commit (tx.ts:648, after
  `endIndexBatch` and `commitVersion`). `tx.ts` takes no image (`takeSavepoint` is imported nowhere in `src/tx/tx.ts`,
  `faces/`, `arr/`). `markBatch` / `undoBatch` are never called by `opSave` / `rollback` (grep over `src/`).
* `restoreSavepoint`: S7's check and message first and unchanged (`… while a batch it was not taken in is open on the
  arena (restore between batches)`), then `if (log !== null) throw new Error('tx: a savepoint is put back while a batch
  is open on the arena (images are put back between batches)')`; `restoreBatchImage`, `wasFaceLive`, `ownerBefore`
  gone; `imagesTaken(p)` by path. Callers of the image in `src/` across the packages: `layout/src/pipeline/runner.ts`

### LINE 2 — the frame's state: CONFIRMED (fixed, pinned)

* (a) the arena half is S8's `markArena` / `undoArena`, `arena/write.ts` byte-identical to its record.
* (b) the index half, read in `frames.ts`: `markIndex` saves the IndexBatchLog's length, `idx.partitions.length`, each
  level's `static` and `tombstones` lengths and `work`'s two counts; `undoIndex` pops the log's writes from its end one
  at a time (`undoWrite`, then `W.pop()`), then the fault hook, then deletes the byKey entry of every partition at or
  above the mark's count, truncates the partition list and the levels' lists, and puts the work counts back.
  `undoWrite`: a tombstone — the key out of its partition's set; an insert — `gridTake`, the key out of its
  partition's pending set, and where it replaced an entry `gridPut(old.key, old.partition, old.box)` and the key into
  the old partition's pending set; a delete — the removed entry put back with its share. Never through `record`.
  The guards (a logged write the index does not hold is skipped) are the author's N-s9-7 for M0-a-14's planted log
  entries; for a real write they never fire (the later writes are undone first, so the index stands as the write left it).
* Every index mutation site of `src/` (grep `gridPut|gridTake|pending.(add|delete|clear)|tombstones[…]|byKey[…]`):

  **The survivors, judged by this checker:**
  - **C37** (the index log cut once after the whole index replay) — EQUIVALENT. Re-applying an already-undone suffix
    of index writes from its end changes nothing: for a key K let S0(K) be its entry at the mark. An insert's undo acts
    only if K's current entry names the write's partition, and then leaves K at the write's old entry (the state before
    that write); otherwise it is skipped and K stays. A delete's undo acts only if K is absent, and then puts its old
    entry back; otherwise K stays. By induction down to K's earliest write in the suffix, whose old entry is S0(K), K
    ends at S0(K) either way, the pending sets following each take and put; a tombstone's undo is a Set delete of a key
    that was not in the set at the mark. No pin can tell — the brief's (g) expected the interrupted-undo pin red for
    "the logs cut only once": it is, for the arena half (C38), where a re-applied entry does corrupt.
  - **C41** — EQUIVALENT at this head: LINE 3 (the golden under the mutant and two probes). Note N-s9c-4.
  - **C50** (the sweep's `[roleTop, role.top)` loop dropped) — EQUIVALENT while every store is logged: a fresh row's
    kind store is a logged column entry, so the row is already in `rolesLogged`. The loop is what keeps the sweep right
    if line 4 (ii) FRESH skipping is ever built (a fresh row's stores would then be unlogged) — said in N-s9c-5.
  - **D12** (the index undo does not put `idx.work`'s two counts back) — EQUIVALENT on every honest path: the counts
    move only in `rebuildPartition`, which no `src/` caller runs inside a batch (LINE 2); a rebuild inside a batch is
    the deliberate-caller case of N-s9c-1, where the counts are the least of what is not undone.

## (3) New findings — judged by the blocker rule

None of the findings below is a blocker: no gate exits non-zero for a reason of the item's (RELATED@1000, the pins and the observer suite are red only on a-09's
six tests, red identically on the RESUME head), no
listed interface or test is missing, no stub or shortcut stands on an honest path, no honest input gives a wrong result
(the golden, the roots, the oracle, the observer suite), nothing is written outside `plat/`, and no firewalled file was
read. They go to `checks/M0-a-06-notes.md` ('Hardening round S9 — the closing check's notes').

* **N-s9c-1** — an index rebuild inside an open batch is not undone by the frames (the before-image restored the
  trees, keys, pending and tombstone sets it rewrites; the door logs only its home-entry stores, so an undo would leave
  the partition's keys naming items whose home entries read −1). No `src/` caller rebuilds inside a batch (LINE 2);
  suggested handling: the debug build's assertion attachIndex gained, on `rebuildPartition` (M0-a-03's file; M4, or
  with amendment z's index round 987).
* **N-s9c-2** — bar (6) in the tiny-tables mode and on the wide families (LINE 5 (e)): for the session's ruling before
  the landing; the figures are LINE 5 (e)'s table (default 24 seeds 124 ≤ 160; wide 182 – 183 with no replacement entry;
  tiny 169 on the 24 seeds, 244 – 269 on the wide families, 38 – 61 replacement entries on the worst batches).
* **N-s9c-3** — the author's L-0794 discloses two slips of the working rules at its start: `git log --oneline -5` and
  `git status --porcelain` run once (read-only), and one non-recursive `ls` of the project root (top-level names only).
  Neither opened, listed or searched a firewalled folder's content, and nothing was written: no clean-room breach
  (rule 1 forbids reading the folders, and the names are the brief's own); recorded here for the session.
* **N-s9c-4** — the commit record's before-owner read (`before.ownerOf`, tx.ts `assemble`) is redundant at this head:
  every writer that re-owns or frees a face logs the owner it had (LINE 3, C41), so no test can pin the read and none
  does. A later writer that re-owns or frees a face without logging would make it load-bearing with no pin: add, with
  such a writer or in the hardening pass, a pin through a test-only writer (or an assertion that the before-owner of a
  dirty face is in `t.log.owners`). M4.
* **N-s9c-5** — three equivalences that hold only under a condition worth a line: C50 (the sweep's fresh-row loop is
  dead code while every store is logged, and is what keeps the sweep right under line 4 (ii) FRESH skipping — whoever
  builds (ii) must pin it); C37 (cutting the index log once would be as correct as the per-write cut that stands, but
  only because `undoWrite`'s guards — added for N-s9-7's planted writes — make a re-applied suffix idempotent: without
  the guards the per-write cut alone carries the resume property, so neither may be dropped on the other's account); D12 (the work counts are restored but nothing in a frame moves them — N-s9c-1's case).
  M4, or with the round that builds line 4.
